resources.string: Made for touch: big controls, a panel that hides, the Phone widget, rounded corners. Heavier (about 1 GB more): best with root.
From the next start. A desktop not used before is installed beside the other first, which takes a few minutes.
Light and quick: the best fit for PRoot.
Stable and light, with Firefox ESR.
Newer packages, with the Falkon browser (Ubuntu\'s Firefox needs Snap, which can\'t run here).
From the next start. Rounded corners, smooth scrolling and animations, drawn on the CPU. Turn them off if the desktop feels slow.
Linux couldn\'t be downloaded. Check the connection, then try again (it carries on where it stopped).
The install didn\'t finish. The lines below say where.
Root isn\'t available. Switch it on in Shell access, then try again.
The built-in shell isn\'t running. Start it in Shell access, then try again.
The desktop didn\'t start. The lines below say why.
From the next start. Programs draw on the phone\'s GPU; the desktop itself stays on the CPU. Turn it off if a program shows black or garbled.
Installing the desktop. This takes a few minutes; you can leave this page.
Downloads Linux (30 to 50 MB) and installs a desktop on it: about 1.5 GB in all with Xfce, 2.5 GB with KDE Plasma.
Full speed. Uses root through Shell access.
Needs root, switched on in Shell access.
Works on any phone through the built-in shell. Slower.
A browser, a terminal, a file manager and the desktop\'s sound. Apps installed with apt (sudo works) stay installed.
That program isn\'t in Linux any more.
Tap one to open it in the desktop; long-press to put it on the home screen.
Linux and everything saved in it are deleted. The phone\'s own files aren\'t touched.
The desktop is running. Back leaves it running; Stop ends it.
From the next start. Bigger suits the phone; 1× suits a large screen.
The desktop has stopped. Press Back.
The desktop turned the password down.
The desktop isn\'t running. Start it from the Desktop page.
The desktop runs through it: with root as a chroot, without through PRoot.

Flux Desktop runs Debian or Ubuntu (downloaded from their own servers) with Xfce or KDE Plasma, through PRoot (as patched by Termux) or a chroot, its programs drawing on the phone’s GPU through virglrenderer and libepoxy. On Debian with KDE Plasma it adds Klassy by Paul McAuley and KDE Rounded Corners by Matin Lotfali. The chroot’s setup, the touch panel and gestures and the Phone widget come from Titan-2-Elite-Debian-Chroot.
